videos.title: The AI unlock has begun
videos.ai_tech_id: Claude Opus 5.5 — used as a reverse-engineering/game-modding agent, alongside Runway for video generation
summary: AI Search covers how AI models, including Claude Opus 5.5, are now being used to mod video games end-to-end: reverse engineering compiled binaries, building pass-through mods, and rebuilding original game logic in Rust.

The video walks through porting mechanics across platforms and demonstrates prompting workflows for cracking software and modding tools, pointing to several open-source repos (universal modders, Ghidra/IDA MCP servers, decompilers) that make this pipeline possible.

It frames this as an inflection point where AI collapses the skill barrier for reverse engineering and modding, segments which previously required deep specialist expertise, and includes a sponsored segment for Runway.

videos.title: Remotion vs  Hyperframes. One prompt. One map skill
videos.ai_tech_id: Remotion Maps (AI video-generation skill) vs. Hyperframes — programmatic/AI video rendering tools
summary: Futurepedia pits Remotion's built-in 'Remotion Maps' skill against Hyperframes using a single shared prompt and task: generate a cinematic map animation that follows real highways with smooth camera movement.

The video shows Remotion Maps taking a natural-language description of a route, map style, and camera motion and rendering it directly into a polished animated video, then checks whether Hyperframes can reproduce the same result from the identical prompt.
It's a head-to-head format aimed at helping creators decide which AI video tool currently handles cinematic, route-based map animation better for content production.

videos.title: I Built Another Andrej Karpathy Using Claude
videos.ai_tech_id: Claude Code — used to build a persona/expert-clone agent from a large personal corpus
summary: Nate Herk builds a Claude Code agent modeled on Andrej Karpathy, trained on over 700,000 words pulled from Karpathy's lectures, blog posts, and social posts so it explains AI concepts the way Karpathy does.

He walks through the 4-step process: compiling the corpus into a personal 'wiki', distilling it into a small set of behavioral rules, assembling the Claude Code agent, and then running and testing it live on-camera.

He frames the technique as generalizable — once you've cloned one expert's teaching style into a Claude Code agent, the same 4 steps can be applied to clone almost any other expert you want to learn from.

videos.title: 10 Secret Codes for ChatGPT and Muse
videos.ai_tech_id: ChatGPT and Meta Muse — used via named output-format prompt commands
summary: Sabrina Ramonov shares 10 short command codes (e.g. MAKE-VISUAL-STUDYGUIDE, MAKE-MINDMAP, QUIZME, ELI5, FEYNMAN-TECHNIQUE, SOCRATES, FIRSTPRINCIPLES) that tell ChatGPT or Muse exactly what output format and teaching method to use instead of relying on open-ended prompting.

Each code maps to a specific study need — visual summaries, mind maps, sticky-note recall, diagrams, one-question-at-a-time quizzing, simplified explanations, prioritized 80/20 review, or first-principles breakdowns — so naming the format upfront produces more consistent answers.
She positions this as a faster alternative to prompt guesswork for students, pointing viewers to a larger paid list of similar 'secret codes' for other use cases beyond studying.
